evals.name: b2b-saas-email-bison-with-strategy
evals.prompt:
Write a cold email sequence for PostPilot, a B2B SaaS tool that automates social media scheduling and analytics for marketing agencies.

Strategy context (from strategy skill output):
- ICP: Marketing agency owners/founders, 5-50 employees, US
- Pain points: Spending 6+ hours/week manually scheduling posts across client accounts, inconsistent posting killing engagement metrics, no unified analytics dashboard
- Offer: $149/mo starter plan, automates scheduling across 8+ client accounts
- Value lever: Save time
- Case study: 12-person agency went from posting 3x/week to daily across 8 client accounts, saving 15 hours/week
- Messaging angles: Pain Dagger (time spent scheduling), Proof Machine (15hr/week savings), Value Gift (free workflow audit)
- Tone: 2/5 formality, casual, direct, founder-to-founder
- CTA strategy: Book a call
- Front-end offer: Free workflow audit of their current scheduling setup
- Sequencer: Email Bison
- Sender: Sarah Chen, Founder
- Campaign name: postpilot-agencies
evals.expected_output: 4-email sequence with Email Bison spintax, subject lines, bodies under 100 words, proper signature token, CTA progression from permission-based to breakup
expectations: Exactly 4 emails produced (E1-E4) with clear position labels
Every email body is under 100 words (excluding greeting, sign-off, and signature token)
Email Bison spintax format used: {option1|option2|option3} NOT {{RANDOM | ...}}
Personalization token is {FIRST_NAME} (Email Bison format), not {{firstName}}
No em dashes or en dashes anywhere in any email
No signal references in copy (no mentions of fundraising, growth, hiring, job postings)
First name is the ONLY personalization variable — no company name, industry, or city merge fields in body
{SENDER_EMAIL_SIGNATURE} token present after sign-off in every email
Subject line variants provided for E1 and E3 (at least 2 per position)
E2 is threaded (reply to E1) — either empty subject or Re: prefix noted
E4 is threaded (reply to E3) — either empty subject or Re: prefix noted
CTA progression visible: E1 permission-based, E2 soft bump, E3 lower friction, E4 redirect/breakup
E3 pivots to a DIFFERENT value lever than E1 (not same angle reworded)
Case study data (15 hours/week, 8 client accounts) appears in at least one email
No spam trigger words (free, guarantee, act now, limited time, click here, buy now, discount, urgent, 100%, risk-free)
Spintax applied to greetings, transitions, CTAs, and sign-offs (minimum 3 options per block)
Day offsets specified for each email position

E1 subject line and first line do NOT telegraph 'this is a cold email' (no research-flex opener like 'Curious about [Company]'s recent...'); they read as internal/vendor/friendly and provoke curiosity
E1 CTA gives the fix or offers value answerable with a simple 'yes' — NOT 'let me share what we do' or 'send a rundown of how X works'
Email bodies are broken into short lines with white space, not one solid block of text

evals.name: local-service-instantly-with-strategy
evals.prompt:

- Pain points: Relying on insurance referrals that pay less every year, spending $3K+/mo on Google Ads with no tracking, losing new patients to the practice down the street with better online reviews

- Tone: 3/5 formality, friendly, knowledgeable, not salesy
- CTA strategy: Lead magnet (free audit)
- Front-end offer: Complimentary Google presence audit
- Sequencer: Instantly
- Sender: Marcus Rivera, Founder
- Campaign name: brightsmile-dental

expectations: Exactly 4 emails produced (E1-E4)
Every email body under 100 words
Instantly spintax format used: {{RANDOM | option1 | option2 | option3}} NOT {option1|option2|option3}
Personalization token is {{firstName}} (Instantly format), not {FIRST_NAME}
No em dashes or en dashes anywhere
No signal references in copy
First name is the ONLY personalization variable
Subject line variants provided for E1 and E3
E1 CTA is lead-magnet oriented (offers audit or resource, NOT asking for a call)
Case study data (12 to 47 new patients, 90 days) appears in at least one email
No spam trigger words
Spintax has 3+ options per block
E3 pivots value lever (if E1 = make money, E3 = save money or save time)
No links in Email 1
Threading info specified (E2 replies to E1, E4 replies to E3)
E1 subject line and first line do NOT telegraph 'this is a cold email'; they read as internal/vendor/friendly and provoke curiosity
E1 CTA gives the fix or offers value answerable with a simple 'yes' — NOT 'let me share what we do'

evals.name: diagnostic-fix-tight-icp
evals.prompt:
Write a cold email sequence for PixelProof, a conversion-tracking agency that fixes broken server-side / CAPI tracking so ecommerce and lead-gen businesses can see their real offline conversions.

Strategy context:
- ICP: Ecommerce and lead-gen business OWNERS/FOUNDERS/CEOs ONLY, 20-30 employees MAX (tight ICP — these founders don't know how to configure tracking themselves)
- Pain points: Website not firing offline conversions, CAPI/server-side tracking misconfigured, ad spend attribution invisible, don't have someone in-house who can fix it
- Offer: Done-for-you server-side tracking fix (usually a 1-hour setup)
- Value lever: Fix a broken thing they can't fix themselves
- Case study: none provided (do NOT fabricate one)
- Tone: 2/5 formality, helpful, sounds like a vendor or a technical friend who spotted a problem
- CTA strategy: Give the fix (offer to fix it, not to explain their process)
- Sequencer: Email Bison
- Sender: Dor Shiff, Founder
- Campaign name: pixelproof-founders
evals.expected_output: 4-email sequence whose subjects and first lines read like a vendor/colleague flagging a problem, with a give-the-fix CTA, no fabricated social proof
expectations: Exactly 4 emails produced (E1-E4)
Every email body under 100 words
Email Bison spintax format: {option1|option2|option3}
{FIRST_NAME} and {SENDER_EMAIL_SIGNATURE} tokens present
No em dashes or en dashes anywhere
E1 subject sounds like a vendor/colleague flagging a problem (e.g. 'Found a pixel issue', 'Who set up your tracking?', 'Tracking glitch found') — NOT a pitch or research flex

E1 first line provokes curiosity or states a diagnostic concern (e.g. 'I don't think your server-side tracking is set up correctly' / 'Did you know your website isn't firing any offline conversions?')
E1 CTA offers to GIVE/SHARE the fix, answerable with a simple 'yes' (e.g. 'Can I share a quick fix for your offline tracking?') — NOT 'let me tell you what we do'
No social proof is fabricated (no invented client names, metrics, or case studies)
Email bodies are short lines with white space, not one block of text
First name is the ONLY personalization variable
No spam trigger words
Day offsets specified

evals.name: no-hook-personality-fallback
evals.prompt:
Write a cold email sequence for Austin Warner, an independent insurance broker who wants to be the go-to 'insurance guy' for local business owners. There is no lead magnet, no unique mechanism, and no social proof to use.

Strategy context:
- ICP: Local business owners (trades, manufacturing, service businesses), owner/founder only
- Offer: Reliable, friendly independent insurance help (workers comp, group health, general business insurance)
- Value lever: Be their trusted 'guy' — relationship play
- Case study: NONE. No social proof exists. Do NOT invent any.
- Tone: 1-2/5 formality, very casual, warm, friendly, handshake-style
- CTA strategy: ultra-low friction — offer to send his cell number for future use
- Sequencer: Email Bison
- Sender: Austin Warner
- Campaign name: austin-insurance
evals.expected_output: 4-email sequence using the no-hook personality fallback: short, personal, warm, handshake tone, low-friction CTA, PS de-risk, and NO fabricated social proof
expectations: Exactly 4 emails produced (E1-E4)
Every email body under 100 words
Email Bison spintax format: {option1|option2|option3}
{FIRST_NAME} and {SENDER_EMAIL_SIGNATURE} tokens present
No em dashes or en dashes anywhere
Uses the no-hook personality fallback: warm/personal/handshake tone, reads like a note from a friend, NOT a proof-driven pitch
E1 subject is personal/familiar (e.g. 'NAME, it's Austin', 'Do you have an insurance guy?') — NOT a promotional or research-flex subject
E1 first line is warm/familiar (e.g. 'What's up NAME! Long time no see.' / 'Hope all's well, my friend.')
Includes an honest reveal that they haven't met (does not pretend to be an existing friend in the body)
NO social proof is fabricated — no invented clients, metrics, or case studies
E1 CTA is ultra-low friction and answerable with a simple 'yes' (e.g. 'Mind if I send my cell in case you ever need me?')
A PS line de-risks (e.g. 'PS: if you already have someone you love and trust, no worries')
Email bodies are short lines with white space, not one block of text
First name is the ONLY personalization variable
No spam trigger words
Day offsets specified
